summary.title: What Sourcegraph learned building AI coding agents
summary.one_liner: Lessons from Sourcegraph's "Raising an Agent" work on building AI coding agents: favor context curation, rich feedback loops, sub-agents, multi-model "oracle" setups, and CI-driven background agents.
keywords: how to build ai coding assistant
takeaways: Give an agent tools and high-level goals rather than micromanaging each step; trust it to orchestrate.
Curate context carefully; use sub-agents with their own context windows so the main agent isn't polluted by noisy intermediate steps.
A worker model handles bulk tool use while a stronger 'oracle' model is consulted for planning and debugging, keeping costs manageable.
Background agents can use existing CI pass/fail output as their feedback loop instead of replicating full local environments.
Practical tips include Playwright for screenshots, simple Storybook-style UI pages, env-var auth bypass for local dev, and giving agents psql access to create seed data.
summary.summary: This is a blog-style reflection on Sourcegraph's work building the Amp coding agent, drawing on the authors' "Raising an Agent" video diary. It covers ideas such as inversion of control, curated rather than maximal context, spawning sub-agents, a worker/oracle multi-model split, and usage-based pricing implications. It also discusses background agents that use CI as feedback and ends with a short list of practical development tips for agent-driven work. The page is opinion and experience rather than a step-by-step tutorial, so the concepts are described qualitatively.
